name: Chained Decline Dumbbell Press
description: A decline dumbbell press with chains attached to the dumbbells and draped on the floor. The decline angle targets the sternal and lower pectoral fibers while the chains provide accommodating resistance — increasing load as the dumbbells rise and chain links lift off the floor. At full lockout, the maximal chain load challenges the peak contraction where free weights typically feel easiest.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a decline bench (15–30 degrees) with feet secured. Attach chains to dumbbells so they drape to the floor from the bottom position. Hold dumbbells at chest level.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure chains to dumbbell handles with carabiners. Adjust chain length so they begin lifting off the floor in the mid-to-upper range of the press. Reduce dumbbell weight to account for the chain addition.
steps: Step 1: Begin at the bottom position with elbows at chest level. Chains drape to the floor.
Step 2: Press the dumbbells upward. Chain links progressively lift as the dumbbells rise.
Step 3: At full lockout, all chains are suspended and the peak load occurs.
Step 4: Lower under control. Chains re-contact the floor, deloading the bottom. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale at the bottom, exhale forcefully through the press.
common_mistakes: Chains that don't engage — means they are too long for the decline setup
Underestimating the total load — count dumbbell plus chain weight when programming
Feet unsecured — always secure feet on the decline
safety_considerations: Secure feet firmly on the decline bench
Use significantly less dumbbell weight than normal to account for chain addition
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from lower chest to lockout. Chain loading is highest at the top.
coaching_cues: Press hard all the way through — the chains reward explosive effort at the top
Feel the bottom deload as the chains hit the floor — that tells you the range of engagement
